national.line: A Florida fitness coach set a Guinness World Record by hip-thrusting 639 pounds. Leg day just got a whole lot scarier.
An orphaned 5-month-old walrus calf, found alone on a remote northern Alaska beach and weighing about 220 pounds, now has a new home at SeaWorld Orlando. That's one big baby.
A giant pumpkin named Rocky gave a champion grower his comeback win in California. Rocky goes the distance again.
A California woman set a Guinness World Record for the largest collection of frog memorabilia. Her house must be hopping.
A little girl entered a talent show without telling her mom, and the crowd loved every second. Confidence level: sky high.
Reacher star Alan Ritchson stunned fans by singing Michael Jackson's Human Nature in his hotel room. Turns out the tough guy has pipes.
A Detroit Free Press writer tried ordering a Starbucks coffee served in a pumpkin, and it actually worked. Peak fall has officially been reached.

pride.label: Hall of Fame
pride.line: Dean Long, Lebanon High School graduate, was inducted into the Emporia State University baseball Hall of Fame in October. Not bad for a kid from Lebanon.

pride.label: Budget Award
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools earned a national Meritorious Budget Award. Somebody over there really knows their spreadsheets.

pride.label: All-District
pride.line: Lilly Bradbury took fourth in singles, and Ava Johnson and Carli Alford took fourth in doubles, earning Lebanon girls tennis three All-District honors in October. That's a lot of racket.

pride.label: New Coach
pride.line: Brittany Stamm was named the new head girls basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools. Time to lace up those sneakers.

pride.label: New Coach
pride.line: Kalem Copling was named the new head boys basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools. The whistle has a new owner.

pride.label: Grand Opening
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools celebrated the opening of the Robert W. Plaster Center for Student Success. Fresh space, big plans.

pride.label: World Food Champs
pride.line: Waynesville Career Center culinary students Molly McDermitt, Cycila Keeney and Samantha Etheridge cooked in the finals of the World Food Championships in Indianapolis on Oct. 18 with a dish called Bacon Lover's Christmas. Bacon for Christmas? Sign us up.

pride.label: Teacher Award
pride.line: Kyleen Oxendine, a teacher at East Elementary in Waynesville, won the first-quarter Project Teach Award on Oct. 19 for her Take Home Reading Success Kits. Homework kids actually want? Genius.

pride.label: Community Award
pride.line: Domino's of Waynesville received the Waynesville school district's Community Recognition Plaque for October on Oct. 19 for supporting students. Pizza really does fix everything.

pride.label: Spirit Trophy
pride.line: The Waynesville Sixth Grade Center won the traveling Tiger Spirit Trophy again for taking first place in the homecoming parade. Sixth graders, setting the bar high.

pride.label: Record Scores
pride.line: Bolivar School District students posted the strongest state test results in district history, with math proficiency at 56.3%, 12.5 points above the state average. Somebody's been doing their homework.

pride.label: Graduates
pride.line: Lathan Martin and Boone Shockley of Grand Missouri Bank in Bolivar graduated from the Oklahoma Bankers Association Consumer Lending School in Oklahoma City in October. Back to school, banker edition.

pride.label: 100 Years
pride.line: Marshfield Chevrolet marked 100 years in business with a two-day celebration in October. A century in, and still rolling.

pride.label: Band Honors
pride.line: The Marshfield High School marching band took fourth place at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival. That's music to our ears.

pride.label: New Leader
pride.line: Keith Klostermann, a 30-year educator, was named the new city administrator for Osage Beach. From the classroom to City Hall.

pride.label: Athlete of the Week
pride.line: Crocker soccer player Johnny Carriger was named KY3 Athlete of the Week after scoring a hat trick in Crocker's district championship game. Three goals, one happy hometown.

pride.label: Cross Country
pride.line: The Macks Creek girls cross country team won the varsity title and the boys finished second at the Dixon Invitational at Oak Hills Golf Course in Dixon in October. Those kids really go the distance.

local.line: Lebanon city street, electric, water and wastewater crews trained with two neighboring cities on Oct. 21 for trench and confined-space rescues. Safety first, second and third.
The Lebanon R-3 Schools Hive Depot is giving Lebanon students essential resources and learning opportunities. A little help goes a long way.
The City of Lebanon proposed another new city logo in October, with a fresh slogan: Build your journey here. Second time's the charm.
A Colonial estate in Lebanon with more than 21,000 square feet on seven-plus acres goes up for online auction in early November, with bidding starting at $995,000. Start checking the couch cushions.
The Joel E. Barber C-5 school district is considering building a high school onto its existing building, Superintendent Dr. Rachelle Jennings said in October. Big plans are on the drawing board.
A historic Route 66 gas station in Marshfield has been restored. Get your kicks, Marshfield.
Fast Food Club named a retro Route 66 diner in St. Robert the Missouri road-trip stop for chicken-fried steak and malts. Save room for the malt.
Two new Missouri State Highway Patrol troopers from the 126th recruit class have been assigned to Camden and Miller counties in Troop F. Mind that speedometer, Lake folks.
A Lake of the Ozarks resort mogul plans to buy and renovate the foreclosed Regalia Hotel. A fresh start, and then some.
The Webster County Health Unit officially launched its Baby Bridge program to help families with babies and toddlers, after a two-month pilot. Parents need all the backup they can get.
The U.S. Census Bureau estimates Seymour now has 2,247 people, and the town keeps growing. Somebody update the welcome sign.
A Seymour man bagged a black bear, one of seven taken in Missouri's Zone 1 by Monday morning of the fall season that opened Saturday. That's one big deer camp story.

music.line: Brothers Osborne released their new album Watertown on Oct. 23, with a duet featuring Cody Johnson called Born and Raised Hell. Three good old boys, one great song.
Ella Langley's Loving Life Again just hit number one on country radio, putting her in elite company with Shania Twain. 2026 really is her year.
Carly Pearce brought out Kelsea Ballerini for two surprise duets at her New York tour finale and called her one of her best friends in the whole world. Besties make the best harmonies.
Morgan Wallen now has his own 24/7 SiriusXM channel, Morgan Wallen Radio, and he curates it himself. All Wallen, all day.
Post Malone, Riley Green, Luke Bryan and Blake Shelton lead the lineup for the Carolina Country Music Fest. That's one stacked weekend.
Trace Adkins and Brantley Gilbert will headline the Boots on the Bayou country music festival. Bring your boots and maybe some bug spray.
The Smithsonian's baby red panda was named Dolly, after the country music icon, in a public vote. Nine to five, nap to snack.

weird.line: A 2,455-pound pumpkin set a new record at the Ohio pumpkin show. That's a whole lot of pie.
A 3,156-pound pumpkin grown in Rhode Island is being inspected for a possible world record. Somebody's going to need a bigger porch.
A message in a bottle written by two little sisters in 1973 was found and returned to them 53 years later. Talk about slow mail.
Authorities in Santa Cruz, California, rounded up a loose emu wandering city streets, just days after catching a different escaped emu. Santa Cruz may need an emu crossing sign.
Neighbors in a Tennessee town are on the lookout for a pet kangaroo that escaped from a property. Just follow the hopping.
A bear wandered into a Florida backyard and raided the fridge for an alcoholic drink, all caught on camera. Bears: they're just like us.
A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton a Montana rancher discovered in 2019 is heading to auction, where it could sell for up to $9 million. Check your back forty, folks.
Scientists discovered a new squid-like species in Wyoming that lived 160 million years ago. Calamari, Jurassic edition.
A mom in Wisconsin stumbled upon the wreckage of a mystery shipwreck. Best walk ever.
Pennsylvania certified a new state record channel catfish, the first new record in 35 years. That's one whiskered giant.
A father-and-son fishing trip might have landed a world-record smallmouth bass. Best dad-and-son day ever.
A moving smoker in Texas, basically a food semi, broke the Guinness record as the largest ever. Barbecue on the go, Texas-style.
A ghostly-looking raccoon in Florida raided a cat's dinner and became an internet star. Trick-or-treat came early this year.
A cow got loose on a Maryland highway. Talk about a moo-ving violation.
Wisconsin costume designer Brandon Johnson built the Spirit Walker, a 9-foot, four-legged creature with a human face, out of thrift-store finds and trash. One man's trash, another man's nightmare.
A four-year-old boy's adorable reaction to hearing his parents' voices for the first time has gone viral. Grab the tissues for this one.
Kyle Berkshire broke his own world record for the longest golf drive. He's only competing with himself now.
Forbes says Gen Z job seekers are showing up to interviews with their parents, iced coffee and AI. Mom, can you take the salary question?
Brooklyn artist Hayden Clay Williams is making stained-glass versions of everyday objects. Fancy enough for a church window.
A new interactive map shows all 1,709 land and sea battles the Romans and their successors fought, starting in 753 BC. Those Romans never took a day off.
A man in Bosnia rescued an abandoned bear cub, and now the two are inseparable. Best buddy ever, with claws.

humor.line: The law behind it, the Fair Labor Standards Act, took effect in 1938 and set a minimum wage of 25 cents. Try buying lunch with that today.
There's even a kind called Lebanon bologna, made in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, since the late 1800s. Wrong Lebanon, but we'll take the credit.
Good and Plenty, the pink and white candy-coated licorice, is the oldest candy brand made in the United States, first made in Philadelphia in 1893. Older than grandma's candy dish.
It's promoted by a possibly satirical British group called the Tripe Marketing Board, and the date comes from a 1662 diary entry about a most excellent dish of tripe. Stomach lining: a love story.
It started in 1975 as a food version of Earth Day, and when it came back in 2011, more than 2,300 events were held. That's a lot of potlucks.
The whole point is to break your normal routine, act a little unhinged and make somebody laugh. So, a regular Saturday at our house.
A Michigan man created it to honor his old roommate on his birthday, and the roommate's last name was Sauer. Some friendships come with a pucker.
Holidays honoring mothers-in-law go back to at least the early 1920s, but this one didn't land on the fourth Sunday of October until the mid-1970s. Call her. Seriously, call her.
The official advice for celebrating: when in doubt, just deep fry any food you have. Your arteries have filed a complaint.
It grew out of the first World Pasta Congress in Rome in 1995, where countries teamed up to get the world eating more pasta. A global plot we fully support.
Pizza making started in Naples in the late 1700s as cheap food for working people. Still the best cheap date.

It marks 1785, when the first Spanish donkeys arrived in Boston as a gift from the King of Spain, and George Washington used them to breed the first mules of their kind in America. Founding Father, founding mule guy.
It comes from a 1769 diary entry, when writer Samuel Johnson was told about a new machine that moved without horses, powered by turning a handle. The first car really did have a crank.

A Dallas public relations man got turned away by the Texas Department of Agriculture and the Texas Beef Council before a state representative helped him make it official. Persistence, with gravy on top.
The word pumpkin comes from the Greek word pepon, which means large melon. Large melon pie just doesn't sound right.
Despite the name, many modern mincemeat recipes don't contain any meat at all. False advertising, holiday edition.
It started in 1922, and October 27 was picked because it's Theodore Roosevelt's birthday. Happy birthday, Teddy, and thank you, sailors.
Potatoes first came to North America with Scotch-Irish immigrants in New Hampshire in 1719, and now they grow in all 50 states. Spud-tacular progress.
The rule is to let your cranky co-workers complain all day long instead of trying to cheer them up. Finally, a day off from fake smiling.
Every wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano ages at least 12 months, and some sit for as long as 40 months. Patience you can grate.
The Statue of Liberty arrived in New York City in 1885 packed in 214 crates and had to be put back together. And you thought flat-pack furniture was hard.
The word chocolate traces back to the Aztec word xocolatl, which means bitter water. Good thing somebody added sugar.
It honors the first public showing of projected moving pictures, Emile Reynaud's Theatre Optique, in 1892. Cartoons have been beating chores ever since.
Wild-food fan Euell Gibbons may have inspired it with his 1962 book, Stalking the Wild Asparagus. Asparagus never stood a chance.
You can even get a plush version of your real-life pet made. Twice the cuddles, none of the shedding.
It marks 1969, when the first electronic message went from one computer to another on ARPANET, the network that led to the internet. People have been arguing online ever since.
It was created by Colleen Paige, the same person behind National Dog Day, and the U.S. has about 90 million house cats. The cats would like to speak to the manager.
Steel-cut oats are sliced thin with steel blades, while rolled oats get steamed and pressed flat. Breakfast has a gym routine.
The Pilgrims learned to make doughnuts in Holland and brought them to New England, and the first ones were literally little nuts of dough. Thank you, Pilgrims.
Breadsticks started in Turin, Italy, in the 1600s, and legend says a court baker named Antonio Brunero created them. Unlimited refills not included.
Candy corn is made from sugar, corn syrup and confectioner's wax. Wax on, wax off, candy corn.
Scientists think lemurs got to Madagascar by floating over from Africa on vegetation. Cheapest cruise ever.
